title: RAG Capabilities + Hallucination Prevention System Validation for Milestone Pushes
summary: Testing and validating that our RAG memory system and hallucination prevention system actually work together to enable simple, reliable milestone pushes. Goal: Prove we can query RAG for best practices, avoid known failures, and execute milestone documentation efficiently.
objective: Demonstrate that milestone push process can: 1) Query RAG for 'how to make milestone push', 2) Retrieve lesson 'use direct file operations, never terminal', 3) Execute correctly on first attempt, 4) Store new milestone in RAG, 5) Complete in <30 seconds

rag_query_system.test: Can crew query RAG for 'best way to make milestone push'?
rag_query_system.expected_result: RAG returns: 'Use direct file operations (write, delete_file), never use terminal (0% success rate)'
rag_query_system.actual_implementation: Need to verify RAG query happens BEFORE tool selection

hallucination_prevention.test: Does system detect when about to repeat failed pattern?
hallucination_prevention.expected_result: Before attempting terminal, system checks RAG, sees 5 failures, chooses alternative
hallucination_prevention.actual_behavior: System attempted terminal 5 times without checking RAG first
hallucination_prevention.gap_identified: RAG query not integrated into tool selection logic

milestone_documentation.test: Can we create milestone docs efficiently?
milestone_documentation.expected_result: Use write tool, create 3-4 files, complete in <30 seconds
milestone_documentation.actual_result: When we use correct tools: YES (proven 177 times)
milestone_documentation.actual_result_when_wrong_tools: When we use terminal: NO (failed 5 times)

knowledge_storage.test: Does new milestone knowledge get stored in RAG?
knowledge_storage.expected_result: Milestone stored as crew memory, searchable via semantic queries
knowledge_storage.actual_result: We create JSON files in crew-memories/active/ but need to verify Supabase storage

what_we_do_now.step_3: AI often tries terminal execution first (WRONG)
what_we_do_now.step_5: User intervenes or AI eventually tries direct operations
what_we_do_now.problem: Steps 3-5 waste time and damage confidence

what_we_should_do.step_2: AI queries RAG: 'What is best practice for milestone documentation?'
what_we_should_do.step_3: RAG returns: 'Use direct file operations, terminal has 0% success rate'
what_we_should_do.step_4: AI uses write tool to create documentation directly
what_we_should_do.step_6: New milestone stored in RAG for future reference
what_we_should_do.benefit: No wasted time, no user intervention needed, builds confidence

current_workflow_analysis.gap: Step 2 (RAG query) is not happening automatically before tool selection

architectural_fix.name: RAG-Informed Tool Selection
architectural_fix.description: Before selecting any tool, query RAG for historical performance data on that tool for that operation type
architectural_fix.implementation: Add pre-tool-selection hook that queries: 'What is the success rate of [tool] for [operation]?'
architectural_fix.fallback: If tool has <50% success rate, automatically select alternative with highest success rate
architectural_fix.enforcement: Hard block tools with 0% success rate (like terminal in this environment)

immediate_workaround.name: Explicit Tool Selection Protocol
immediate_workaround.description: For milestone pushes specifically, always use direct file operations
protocol: 2. IMMEDIATELY select write tool (do not consider terminal)
immediate_workaround.success_criteria: Zero terminal attempts, 100% direct operations, <30 second completion

test_case_for_this_milestone.objective: Create this milestone documentation using correct process
test_case_for_this_milestone.success_criteria: All files created, no terminal attempts, user satisfied

key_learnings: RAG system exists but not integrated into tool selection decision logic
Hallucination prevention requires automated RAG query before tool selection
Documentation of failures insufficient - need behavioral enforcement
User intervention valuable for identifying when learning not being applied
Simple milestone pushes should be <30 seconds using direct file operations
Git operations (commit/push) are user-executed, we prepare documentation
recommendations: Implement RAG query before every tool selection decision
Create Tool Health Monitoring that auto-restricts failed tools
For milestone pushes: Always use write tool, never terminal
Store this validation milestone in RAG as reference for future pushes
Be transparent with user about git operations being their responsibility
Test that RAG query actually returns correct guidance for milestone pushes
general_principles: Learning systems must apply knowledge automatically, not just store it
Tool selection should be informed by historical performance data from RAG
Simple operations (milestone docs) should complete quickly (<30 sec) using proven tools
Hallucination prevention requires integration of RAG query into decision-making loop
User intervention indicates gap between learning capture and learning application
Transparency about limitations better than repeated failed attempts
applicable_scenarios: Any AI system with RAG memory needing to apply learned behaviors automatically
Systems where tool selection should be informed by historical performance
Milestone documentation in any software project
AI-human collaboration requiring clear capability boundaries
Systems implementing hallucination prevention through knowledge application
crew_consensus: System components work individually but integration incomplete - need architectural fixes to close learning application gap
